title: Escape From Dulce - The Hidden Shrine of Umugatu - Part Three - Finale
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RhUoPPchFBU

Daniel (@dungeondive) closes out *The Hidden Shrine of Umugatu* with a total party wipe, and he is entirely good-humoured about it. Picking up from Reginald's disastrous mushroom-induced fungal trap, the mutant commander proceeds to roll two critical hits in a row, then chains claw swipes, tentacle slams and a radiation blast that leaves both heroes on two health with nothing left to heal.

Amelia Earhart dies first. Reginald works out the arithmetic and finds it hopeless: he is melee-only, so reaching the commander means standing inside the radiation blast, and the respawn rules on levels five and six return a dead character with a rusty pipe and nothing else — a weapon that would need a critical hit every single turn to matter. Daniel calls it, house-rules acknowledged, and marks the game with an asterisk.

The post-mortem is the most useful part. He argues the game's one real design failure is boss and mini-boss scaling: everything else adjusts to player count, but commanders do not, leaving two heroes with level-one gear facing a mathematically unwinnable fight. He then draws the Umugatu boss card he never reached — twenty health, three armour, three attacks, and a thrall-summoning power that *does* scale to player count — as proof the designers knew how. He signs off pondering *Deep Madness* next.

----

Should a co-op dungeon crawl always scale its bosses to party size, or is an occasionally unwinnable fight part of the genre's honesty?
